2-5.title: Shape Hunt!
2-5.description: Circles, Squares, and Triangles! Let's find them everywhere!

en.title: Shape Hunt!
en.welcome: Put on your Shape Glasses! (Make circles with hands). We are going on a Shape Hunt! The world is made of shapes!
en.mainContent:
**Circle:** Round like a ball. No corners! It rolls! 
*   Look! A clock is a circle. A cookie is a circle. The moon is a circle!

**Square:** Four sides. One, two, three, four. All the same size. Boxy!
*   Look! A window is a square. A cracker is a square.

**Triangle:** Three sides. Pointy like a pizza slice! 
*   Look! A roof is a triangle. A sandwich cut in half is a triangle.

**Rectangle:** Like a square that got stretched! Two long sides, two short sides.
*   Look! A door is a rectangle. A book is a rectangle.

**3D Shapes (Fat Shapes):**
*   **Sphere:** A ball.
*   **Cube:** A block.
*   **Cone:** An ice cream cone!

**Patterns:** Circle, Square, Circle, Square... what comes next? CIRCLE! You are a math genius!
keyPoints: Circles are round; Squares have 4 sides; Triangles have 3 sides
Rectangles are stretched squares
3D shapes are fat (Sphere, Cube, Cone)
Shapes are everywhere in the world
Patterns repeat (Circle, Square, Circle...)
interactionPrompts: Find something CIRCLE in your room. Point to it!
Make a Triangle with your fingers.
What shape is a door? (Rectangle!)
en.wisdomMoment: Math is not just numbers; it is shapes and patterns. The world is a beautiful puzzle.
en.core_metaphor: The world is built of blocks
en.cta: Draw a 'Shape Monster.' Use a square head, circle eyes, and triangle teeth!
en.summary: You learned about Circles, Squares, Triangles, Rectangles, 3D Shapes, and Patterns!

phases.content: Circle, Square, Triangle, Rectangle, 3D, and Patterns.

6-12.title: Geometry: Measuring the World
6-12.description: Perimeter, Area, Volume, and Angles. How to measure space

en.title: Geometry: Measuring the World
en.welcome: Geometry means 'Earth Measure.' Ancient Egyptians used it to measure farms. Today, we use it to build houses, design video games, and fly rockets.
en.mainContent:
**Perimeter:** The distance AROUND a shape. Imagine walking around a fence. 
*   *Formula:* Add up all the sides. (Side + Side + Side + Side).

**Area:** The space INSIDE a shape. Imagine covering the floor with tiles.
*   *Formula (Rectangle):* Length x Width.

**Volume:** The space inside a 3D object. How much water fits in the box?
*   *Formula (Box):* Length x Width x Height.

**Angles:** How sharp is the corner?
*   **Right Angle (90°):** Like the corner of a book. Perfect L shape.
*   **Acute Angle:** Smaller than 90°. Sharp and pointy! (Cute little angle).
*   **Obtuse Angle:** Bigger than 90°. Wide and open.

**Triangles:** The strongest shape! Bridges are made of triangles because they don't squish easily.

**Symmetry:** If you fold a shape in half, do the sides match? 
*   A butterfly is symmetrical. 
*   Your face is (mostly) symmetrical.

**Pi (π):** A magic number! 3.14... It helps us measure Circles. If you know the distance across a circle (Diameter), multiply by Pi to get the distance around (Circumference).
keyPoints: Perimeter is around; Area is inside; Volume is 3D space
Angles can be Right (90°), Acute (Small), or Obtuse (Big)
Triangles are the strongest shape for building
Symmetry means matching sides
Pi (3.14) is the magic number for circles
interactionPrompts: Look at the corner of the room. Is it a Right Angle?
If a rug is 2 feet wide and 3 feet long, what is the Area? (2x3=6)
Why do you think bridges use triangles instead of squares?
en.wisdomMoment: Nature loves geometry. Honeycombs are hexagons. Snowflakes are hexagons. Flowers are spirals. Math is the language of nature.
en.cta: Find 3 Right Angles in your room. (Hint: Look at books, windows, screens).
en.summary: You've learned about Perimeter, Area, Volume, Angles (Right/Acute/Obtuse), Triangles, Symmetry, and Pi.

13-17.title: Advanced Geometry: Proofs & Pythagoras
13-17.description: Logic, deductive reasoning, and the most famous theorem in math

en.title: Advanced Geometry: Proofs & Pythagoras
en.welcome: Geometry isn't just about shapes; it's about Logic. It was the first system of 'Proof.' You can't just say it's true; you have to PROVE it.
en.mainContent:
**The Pythagorean Theorem:** $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$. 
*   For any Right Triangle, the square of the two short sides (legs) equals the square of the long side (hypotenuse).
*   *Use:* GPS uses this to find your location. Builders use it to make sure corners are square.

**Euclid's Axioms:** Euclid (Greek guy) built all of geometry on 5 simple truths (Axioms). 
*   Example: 'You can draw a straight line between any two points.'
*   From these simple truths, he proved complex things. This is **Deductive Reasoning**.

**Proofs:** A step-by-step argument. 
1.  Statement.
2.  Reason.
3.  Therefore...
This is how lawyers and programmers think. Geometry trains your brain to be logical.

**The Golden Ratio (Phi):** 1.618... A number that appears in nature (shells, pinecones) and art (Mona Lisa). It is considered aesthetically pleasing.

**Fractals:** Shapes that look the same at any scale. Zoom in on a snowflake, and the tip looks like the whole flake. Nature is fractal (trees, rivers, lungs).

**Coordinate Geometry (Descartes):** Combining Algebra and Geometry. Using a grid (X and Y axis) to describe shapes with equations. This is how computer graphics work!
keyPoints: Pythagorean Theorem ($a^2 + b^2 = c^2$) relates sides of a right triangle
Euclid built geometry on Axioms and Deductive Reasoning
Proofs train logical thinking
The Golden Ratio and Fractals appear in nature and art
Coordinate Geometry links Algebra and Shapes (X, Y grid)
interactionPrompts: If a triangle has sides 3 and 4, how long is the hypotenuse? ($3^2+4^2 = 9+16 = 25$. Sqrt(25) = 5!)
Where have you seen a spiral in nature?
Why is logic important for a lawyer?
en.wisdomMoment: There is no Royal Road to Geometry. (Euclid). You have to do the work to understand the truth.
en.cta: Draw a 'Fractal Tree.' Draw a Y. Then on each tip, draw a smaller Y. Keep going.
en.summary: You've explored Pythagorean Theorem, Euclid's Axioms, Proofs, Golden Ratio, Fractals, and Coordinate Geometry.

18-35.title: Non-Euclidean Geometry: Bending Reality
18-35.description: When parallel lines meet, topology, and the shape of the universe

en.title: Non-Euclidean Geometry: Bending Reality
en.welcome: Euclid said parallel lines never meet. He was wrong. (Or rather, he was only right on a flat surface). Welcome to the geometry of curved space, where triangles have more than 180 degrees.
en.mainContent:
**Euclidean vs. Non-Euclidean:**
*   **Flat (Euclidean):** Parallel lines never meet. Triangles = 180°. (Paper).
*   **Spherical (Riemannian):** Parallel lines meet (think longitude lines meeting at the North Pole). Triangles > 180°. (Earth).
*   **Hyperbolic (Lobachevskian):** Parallel lines diverge. Triangles < 180°. (Saddle shape).

**Topology:** The 'Rubber Sheet' geometry. A coffee mug and a donut are the same shape (Topologically) because they both have one hole. You can stretch the mug into the donut without tearing it. 
*   *Joke:* A topologist is someone who can't tell their donut from their coffee cup.

**Dimensions:**
*   **0D:** A point.
*   **1D:** A line.
*   **2D:** A square (Flatland).
*   **3D:** A cube (Us).
*   **4D:** A Tesseract (Hypercube). We can't see it, but we can use math to describe it. Imagine a shadow of a 3D object is 2D. The shadow of a 4D object is 3D.

**The Shape of the Universe:** Is the universe flat, spherical, or hyperbolic? Measurements suggest it is remarkably flat. This is a major mystery in cosmology.

**Graph Theory:** The math of networks. How to connect cities with the shortest roads? How does Google Maps find the route? It's all nodes and edges.
keyPoints: Euclid is only right on flat surfaces; Spherical/Hyperbolic geometry breaks the rules
Topology studies properties preserved under stretching (Donut = Coffee Cup)
We live in 3D, but math can describe 4D+ (Hypercubes)
The Universe appears to be Flat (Euclidean)
Graph Theory powers GPS and Social Networks
interactionPrompts: Imagine living on a sphere. If you walk straight, where do you end up?
Can you visualize a 4D object? (It's okay, nobody really can!)
How many holes does a straw have? (Topologically, it's 1 long hole).
en.wisdomMoment: The universe is written in the language of mathematics. (Galileo). To understand the book, you must learn the language.
en.cta: Watch a video of a 'Rotating Tesseract.' It will melt your brain (in a good way).
en.summary: You've explored Non-Euclidean Geometry, Topology (Donut/Mug), Dimensions (4D), Shape of the Universe, and Graph Theory.

36-60.title: Sacred Geometry: Patterns of Creation
36-60.description: The intersection of math, art, and spirituality

en.title: Sacred Geometry: Patterns of Creation
en.welcome: From the spiral of a galaxy to the spiral of a nautilus shell, the universe repeats the same patterns. Sacred Geometry explores the spiritual meaning behind these forms.
en.mainContent:
**The Flower of Life:** A pattern of overlapping circles that contains all other shapes. Found in ancient temples in Egypt, China, and India. It represents the unity of all life.

**The Golden Ratio (Phi):** 1.618. The 'Divine Proportion.' It creates the Golden Spiral. 
*   Found in: Hurricanes, Pinecones, Sunflowers, Human Faces, The Parthenon.
*   Why? It is the most efficient way to pack seeds or grow leaves. Nature is a mathematician.

**Platonic Solids:** The 5 perfect 3D shapes (Tetrahedron, Cube, Octahedron, Dodecahedron, Icosahedron). Ancient Greeks believed they represented the elements (Fire, Earth, Air, Ether, Water).

**Fractals:** 'As above, so below.' The branching of a tree matches the branching of a river matches the branching of your veins. The microcosm reflects the macrocosm.

**Mandala:** A geometric design used for meditation. Creating or looking at a mandala centers the mind. It represents the order of the universe.

**Architecture:** Cathedrals and Mosques use sacred geometry to create a feeling of awe. The proportions resonate with our bodies and souls.
keyPoints: Sacred Geometry finds spiritual meaning in math patterns
The Flower of Life represents unity
The Golden Ratio (Phi) is nature's efficiency code
Fractals show the connection between Microcosm and Macrocosm
Mandalas and Architecture use geometry to induce peace
interactionPrompts: Why do you think humans find symmetry beautiful?
Look at your hand. Can you see the Golden Ratio in your finger joints?
Does looking at a Mandala make you feel calm?
en.wisdomMoment: Mathematics is the alphabet with which God has written the universe. (Galileo). Look for the signature.
en.core_metaphor: The universe is a geometric dance
en.cta: Draw a Mandala. Start with a dot. Draw a circle. Keep adding layers. Don't plan it; let it grow.
en.summary: You've explored The Flower of Life, Golden Ratio, Platonic Solids, Fractals, Mandalas, and Sacred Architecture.

61-102.title: The Geometry of Aging: Circles and Spirals
61-102.description: Viewing life not as a line, but as a cycle

en.title: The Geometry of Aging: Circles and Spirals
en.welcome: We often think of life as a line (Birth to Death). But nature works in circles (Seasons, Orbits). Aging is not the end of the line; it is the closing of the circle.
en.mainContent:
**Linear vs. Cyclical Time:**
*   **Linear:** Progress. Getting somewhere. 'I must achieve X by age Y.' Stressful.
*   **Cyclical:** Return. Renewal. 'Winter comes, then Spring.' Peaceful.

**The Spiral:** You are not just going in circles (repeating mistakes). You are moving in a Spiral. You pass the same point (a season, a memory), but you are at a higher level of wisdom. You see it differently this time.

**Full Circle:** In elderhood, we often return to the joys of childhood. Play, curiosity, napping, honesty. We become 'twice-born' children, but with wisdom.

**Center of the Wheel:** In youth, we are on the rim of the wheel, spinning fast, covering ground. In age, we move toward the center. The movement slows, but the perspective widens. The center is the point of stillness.

**Fractal Legacy:** Your life is a pattern that repeats in your children and your community. You are a seed that contains the forest.

**Completing the Shape:** A half-drawn circle feels unfinished. Closing the circle (making peace, finishing business) brings a sense of aesthetic and spiritual satisfaction.
keyPoints: Life is a Cycle/Spiral, not just a Line
The Spiral means revisiting the past with new wisdom
Elderhood returns us to the simplicity of childhood (Full Circle)
Moving from the Rim (Action) to the Center (Being)
Closing the circle brings peace
interactionPrompts: Do you feel like you are 'going in circles' or 'spiraling up'?
What childhood joy have you rediscovered recently?
How does it feel to be closer to the 'Center of the Wheel'?
en.wisdomMoment: We shall not cease from exploration, and the end of all our exploring will be to arrive where we started and know the place for the first time. (T.S. Eliot).
en.cta: Draw a spiral. Start wide and go in. Or start in and go wide. Feel the movement.
en.summary: You've explored Linear vs. Cyclical Time, The Spiral, Full Circle, Center of the Wheel, and Completing the Shape.
